title: Palindrome Partitioning IV
spaceBreakdown:
- string t (transformed string): 2n+1 chars → O(n)
- vector<int> rad (Manacher radii): 2n+1 ints → O(n)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input string s, returned bool
approach: Use Manacher's algorithm to compute palindrome radii for the transformed string `#s[0]#s[1]#...#s[n-1]#` in O(n) time and O(n) space. A substring `s[l..r]` is a palindrome iff `rad[l+r+1] >= r-l`. Then enumerate the two cut points: outer loop picks the end `i` of the first part (checking `isPal(0,i)`), inner loop picks the end `j` of the second part (checking `isPal(i+1,j)` and `isPal(j+1,n-1)`). Return true on the first valid triple. This is O(n²) time, O(n) space.
hints: For a string of length up to 2000, there are roughly 2 million ways to place two cuts - what property of each of the three resulting pieces must you verify, and can you afford to check it character-by-character every time? The constraints allow s.length up to 2000.

Use Manacher's algorithm to compute, for every center in the transformed string, the palindrome radius in O(n) time and O(n) space. For s = "abcbdd", the transformed string is "#a#b#c#b#d#d#"; the radius at center 5 (the 'c') is 3, so s[1..3] = "bcb" is a palindrome because 3 ≥ 3−1 = 2.

**Minimum length (n=3)** - every single character is trivially a palindrome.
`Input: "abc"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: outer loop `i < n-3` instead of `i <= n-3` → loop body never executes, returns false.

**Third part is a single character** - last palindrome is just s[n-1].
`Input: "aba"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: inner loop `j < n-2` instead of `j <= n-2` → skips j=n-2, never checks third part of length 1, returns false.

**Center index off by one** - Manacher radii are indexed by center position in the transformed string.
`Input: "abcbdd"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: isPal uses `rad[l+r]` instead of `rad[l+r+1]` → for "bcb" (l=1, r=3), checks rad[4]=0 instead of rad[5]=3, reports not a palindrome, returns false.

**No valid partition** - must exhaust all splits before concluding false.
`Input: "bcbddxy"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: returning true as soon as isPal(0,i) holds for any i, without checking the other two parts → returns true.

followUps.q: What if you need to split into exactly k palindromic substrings instead of 3?
followUps.a: Use DP: dp[i] = minimum number of palindromic substrings to partition s[0..i], computed as min over all j ≤ i where s[j..i] is a palindrome of dp[j-1]+1. With Manacher's O(1) queries, this is O(n²) time and O(n) space. Return dp[n-1] ≤ k.

The O(n²) cut-pair enumeration is too slow. Collect all valid prefix-palindrome ends and suffix-palindrome starts via Manacher (each O(n) to enumerate). For each prefix end i, check if any suffix start j > i+1 yields a palindromic middle s[i+1..j-1]. Early-exit on first match gives O(n) for easy inputs, but worst case remains O(n²); a palindromic tree (eertree) can reduce this to O(n log n).

followUps.q: What if n is divisible by 3 and all three parts must have equal length?
followUps.a: The cut points are fixed at n/3 and 2n/3. Run Manacher once (O(n) time, O(n) space), then check three O(1) queries: isPal(0, n/3-1), isPal(n/3, 2n/3-1), isPal(2n/3, n-1). Total O(n) time, O(n) space.
